claims.statement: JWT tokens carry sub, type (access|refresh), ver (user version bumped on disable/delete), and runtime iat/exp; access expires in 60 minutes, refresh in 14 days, and decode runs on a worker thread via asyncio.to_thread so argon2 / jose do not block the event loop.
Settings.model_post_init refuses to boot when app_env != "development" and jwt_secret equals the committed dev default, so production cannot sign admin JWTs with a publicly known key.

Auth routes apply Redis-backed rate limits: login 10/60s per IP, forgot-password 5/300s per IP and 3/900s per email, reset-password 10/300s per IP and 10/900s per email, refresh 20/60s per IP, reflecting the cost of argon2 verify on the 2 vCPU droplet.

Two roles live in `backend/app/identity/domain/role.py` as `Role(str, Enum)` with values `admin` and `recruiter`. The same names are re-exported as string constants `ADMIN_ROLE = "admin"` and `RECRUITER_ROLE = "recruiter"` in `backend/app/access/domain/policies.py` so the access layer never imports the identity enum. `require_admin` accepts only `admin`; `require_recruiter` accepts both `admin` and `recruiter` — admins implicitly pass every recruiter gate. The role check raises `AccessDeniedError`, translated by the FastAPI dependency to `HTTP 403`. The framework-free split (identity enum → access string constants → `application/roles.py` helpers → FastAPI dependency) keeps RBAC testable without spinning up FastAPI.

`backend/app/api/installation_dependencies.py` provides three layers of post-auth gating: `get_active_installation` resolves the active installation row after `get_current_user`; `require_capability(capability_id)` gates a route on a single capability registered in the capability registry (the id is validated against the registry at dependency-construction time, so an unknown id raises `ValueError` at app startup, not per request); `require_capability_or_legacy(capability_id)` returns the capability if active, otherwise falls back to the legacy resolver (returning `None` instead of raising) so pre-capability callers keep working during a migration. The capability registry is the modern, code-reviewed replacement for the plain "is installed" gate.

CapabilityRegistry rejects duplicate capability ids and duplicate routes/resources/slots inside one capability, validates dependency closure, and resolve() rejects mismatched PACK_CONTRACT_SCHEMA_VERSION, SUPPORTED_KERNEL_ABI, pack version, and pack_contract_hash so stale callers cannot bind to a moved contract.

The recruitment pack declares conversation, knowledge, candidate_intake, job_advisory, and channel.zalo; the candidate_intake capability carries the source-owned DESCRIPTOR, while the shipped recruitment_v1_contract.json is the canonical non-executable parity artifact (schema_version=1, contract_hash 2a7c602a...).

Adapters are reachable through registry.resolve() but never appear in export_pack_contract(); the parity test asserts the shipped JSON equals the export and contains no "import" / "factory" strings, locking the contract surface.

`frontend/src/components/atomic-crm/providers/commons/canAccess.ts` applies three filters before returning `true`: (1) the action must be one of the known react-admin verbs (`list`, `show`, `create`, `edit`, `delete`, `read`, `write`); (2) the resource must be present in `availableResources`, the set compiled at app boot from the static capability runtime — resources the app does not know about cannot be accessed at the UI layer even if the backend gate would allow them; (3) admins pass through, recruiters see `conversations` and `projects` only. The comment in `canAccess.ts` is explicit: "Real enforcement is the FastAPI backend (`app/api/dependencies.py`); this is the UX layer."

`code-review-graph detect-changes` flagged the following functions as modified without a direct test in the new surface: `login`, `reset_password`, `change_password`, `get_user_from_token` (modified, untested), `require_admin` and `require_recruiter` (reached only through a caller). Integration tests for the auth lifecycle live under `backend/tests/`; new tests that exercise the modified helpers directly should land before the corresponding code paths are considered covered.
